In addition to the [[2026–27 Premier League|domestic league]], Manchester City is also participating in the [[2026–27 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2026–27 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], [[2026 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] and [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], entering the latter for the 16th consecutive season. This is the club's first season since [[2015–16 Manchester City F.C. season|2015–16]] without [[Pep Guardiola]] as manager following his resignation at the conclusion of the previous campaign.{{#invoke:cite|news|title=Guardiola to step down after incredible decade as City Manager |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/pep-guardiola-official-announcement-63915039|access-date=22 May 2026|date=22 May 2026|publisher=Manchester City F.C.}} He was replaced with [[Enzo Maresca]] in June 2026.{{cite news |title=City appoint Enzo Maresca as manager |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/enzo-maresca-manchester-city-manager-63918331 |access-date=29 June 2026 |publisher=Manchester City F.C. |date=29 June 2026}} It is also the first season since 2015–16 not to feature [[John Stones]], the first since [[2016–17 Manchester City F.C. season|2016–17]] not to feature [[Bernardo Silva]], and the first since [[2018–19 Manchester City F.C. season|2018–19]] not to feature [[Rodri]], who all departed that summer. City were beaten 3–0 by [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the [[2026 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] on 16 August,{{cite web |last=Begley |first=Emlyn |title=Arsenal 3-0 Man City LIVE: Gunners cruise to Community Shield win as Enzo Maresca's side struggle |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cv4g34g19p2kt |access-date=20 August 2026 |website=BBC Sport}} but went onto record five straight wins in the league to begin the season. alt. }} |} == Season summary == ===Pre-season=== Manchester City began their preparations for the 2026–27 campaign with the appointment of [[Enzo Maresca]] as manager on 29 June 2026, succeeding Pep Guardiola following his departure at the end of the previous season.{{#invoke:cite|news|title=Maresca appointed as new Manchester City manager|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/enzo-maresca-appointed-city-manager-63920001|publisher=Manchester City F.C.|date=28 June 2026|access-date=1 July 2026}} Maresca's arrival marked the beginning of a transitional summer, with the club expected to reshape key areas of the squad after the exits of long-serving players John Stones and Bernardo Silva. City's pre-season planning was shaped significantly by the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], with a large portion of the first-team squad involved in the knockout stages of the tournament, including key figures such as [[Erling Haaland]], [[Rodri]] and [[Jérémy Doku]]; resulting in staggered returns to training and a reduced senior group available for the opening weeks of pre-season.{{#invoke:cite|news|title=World Cup commitments delay City squad's pre-season return|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13165001/man-city-world-cup-players-knockout-stages|publisher=Sky Sports|date=28 June 2026|access-date=1 July 2026}} In all, six first team players remained in competition with England, Spain and France in the final week of competition. Transfer activity during June and early July focused on reinforcing the defensive line and adding depth in midfield, with City linked to multiple right-backs and a progressive midfielder suited to Maresca's possession-focused approach.{{#invoke:cite|news|title=Manchester City assess defensive options ahead of Maresca's first season|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/10/manchester-city-transfer-news-maresca|publisher=The Guardian|date=10 June 2026|access-date=1 July 2026}} The club also monitored potential additions in wide attacking positions, aiming to increase flexibility across the forward line.{{#invoke:cite|news|title=City exploring forward reinforcements as pre-season begins|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66102011|website=BBC Sport|date=12 June 2026|access-date=1 July 2026}} A major development in early July was the imminent signing of [[Elliot Anderson]] from [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], with reports indicating that City had agreed a club-record fee of £116 million for the midfielder as part of Maresca's restructuring of the squad.{{#invoke:cite|news|title=Manchester City close in on Elliot Anderson in record deal|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/06/30/manchester-city-elliot-anderson-transfer-record-fee|publisher=The Daily Telegraph|date=30 June 2026|access-date=1 July 2026}} The club later confirmed the transfer was agreed, and formalities were completed when the player returned from his World Cup duties on 23 July. Following his [[FIFA World Cup Golden Ball|Golden Ball]]-winning performances at the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], where he'd captained [[Spanish national football team|Spain]] to their second title, [[Rodri]] was widely linked with a return to [[La Liga]] during the summer transfer window. Reports in Spanish and English media suggested interest from both Real Madrid and Barcelona, with negotiations involving Madrid reportedly stalling in late July before [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] intensified their pursuit. Manchester City maintained that Rodri was not for sale, though several outlets claimed the club might consider a transfer in the final year of his contract, with figures between £60m and €75m mentioned. Barcelona were also reported to have agreed personal terms with the player, while Real Madrid explored reviving their interest.{{cite news |title=Rodri linked with Spain return after World Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/clyj1rgdnpxo |website=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2026 |access-date=7 August 2026}} The deal with Barcelona was eventually concluded on 18 August for a reported fee of around £65 million. === Start of season === Manchester City began the season with a 3–0 defeat to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the [[2026 FA Community Shield|Community Shield]] at the [[Millennium Stadium|Principality Stadium]], marking Enzo Maresca's first competitive match in charge. Arsenal struck inside 23 seconds through [[Riccardo Calafiori]] before [[Kai Havertz]] doubled the lead with a header midway through the first half. [[Martin Ødegaard]] added a third shortly after the interval, finishing a move created by [[Christos Tzolis]], who impressed with two assists. City created chances through [[Phil Foden]] and [[Antoine Semenyo]] but were unable to beat [[David Raya]], suffering their heaviest Community Shield loss since losing by the same score-line to Arsenal in [[2014 FA Community Shield|2014]]. As the 2026 summer transfer window moved into its final days, Manchester City oversaw a significant reshaping of the squad with several senior departures and targeted reinforcements. Winger [[Savinho]] completed a club-record move to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], while midfielder [[Tijjani Reijnders]] left for [[Saudi Pro League]] side [[Al Qadsiah FC|Al-Qadsiah]] after just one season in Manchester. Forward [[Omar Marmoush]] also moved towards the exit, with a loan deal agreed for him to join Tottenham as part of the London club’s late-window attacking rebuild. Meanwhile, midfielder [[Nico González (footballer, born 2002)|Nico González]] was made available for transfer and subsequently departed for [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle]] as City continued their broader midfield restructuring. City simultaneously strengthened key areas of the squad. Teenage central midfielder [[Ayyoub Bouaddi]] arrived from [[Lille OSC|Lille]] in a major deal reflecting the club’s long-term recruitment strategy, while World Cup-winning midfielder [[Enzo Fernández]] joined from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on a record breaking fee, in one of the window’s most notable Premier League transfers; adding immediate quality and depth to Enzo Maresca’s central options. The club also secured the signing of Brazilian winger [[Allan (footballer, born 2004)|Allan]] from [[SE Palmeiras|Palmeiras]], viewed as a versatile addition capable of operating both as a winger and attacking wing back; and Senegalese winger [[Iliman Ndiaye]] from [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] to add further quality in wide areas. [[Jack Grealish]] left on loan to Everton for the second consecutive season for the final year of his City contract. City started their season strongly, maintaining a 100% winning record in five league fixtures and their opening matches in both the EFL Cup and UEFA Champions League by the time of the international break at the end of September. This run placed them top of the early Premier League table, three points clear of Arsenal. ===Decision of the independent commission into financial irregularities=== In late September 2026, multiple reports revealed Manchester City had been found guilty of 114 charges related to breaching the Premier League's financial regulations between 2009 to 2018.{{cite news |title=Man City found guilty on all but one of 115 charges, reports say, with appeal expected |url= |work=Reuters |date=25 September 2026}} An independent commission concluded the club did not accurately report its finances - including by inflating sponsorship contracts to disguise owner funding - improperly structured or insufficiently disclosed manager and player remuneration figures,{{cite news |title=Manchester City found guilty of majority of Premier League financial breaches charges, according to reports |url= |work=CNN |date=25 September 2026}} such as those related to image‑rights payments,{{cite news |title=Manchester City reportedly found guilty of almost 115 financial charges |url= |work=Al Jazeera |date=25 September 2026}} and failed to co-operate with League's investigation or comply with
